name: @focusgts/aep-mcp-server

tools.name: aep_list_schemas
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Schemas · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List XDM schemas from the Adobe Experience Platform Schema Registry. Returns a lightweight, paginated list (IDs and titles) for the tenant or global container.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100)

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination

containerType.description: Schema registry container: 'tenant' for org-specific schemas, 'global' for Adobe-defined schemas

tools.name: aep_get_schema
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Schemas · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Get the full XDM schema definition by its $id (or meta:altId) from the Adobe Experience Platform Schema Registry. Returns the resolved schema including allOf composition, properties, and meta fields.

tools.name: aep_create_schema
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Schemas · write · Sandbox-scoped]

Create a new XDM schema in the tenant container of the Adobe Experience Platform Schema Registry. Extends a standard XDM class (e.g. Profile, ExperienceEvent) via classRef, and composes in zero or more field groups via fieldGroupRefs.

IMPORTANT: a schema built from a class alone carries only that class's base fields — it has NO tenant-specific fields and is rarely useful on its own. Supply 'fieldGroupRefs' with the field groups that actually carry your data (e.g. 'https://ns.adobe.com/xdm/context/profile-person-details'). Field groups can also be added later with 'aep_update_schema'.

Returns the created schema including its generated $id.

title.description: Human-readable title for the schema (e.g. 'Loyalty Profile')

description.description: Optional description of the schema's purpose

classRef.description: The $ref URI of the XDM class to extend (e.g. 'https://ns.adobe.com/xdm/context/profile' or 'https://ns.adobe.com/xdm/context/experienceevent')

fieldGroupRefs.description: Array of XDM field group $ref URIs to compose into the schema. Field groups are what give a schema its actual fields. Example: ['https://ns.adobe.com/xdm/context/profile-person-details', 'https://ns.adobe.com/xdm/context/profile-personal-details']. Omit ONLY if you intend a bare class-based schema with no additional fields.

tools.name: aep_update_schema
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Schemas · write · Sandbox-scoped]

Update an existing XDM schema in the Adobe Experience Platform Schema Registry using JSON Patch. The most common use is ADDING FIELD GROUPS to a schema that was created without them — a schema built from a class alone has no tenant-specific fields.

Two ways to call this:
  1. 'addFieldGroupRefs' — convenience form. Appends each field group to the schema's allOf array.
  2. 'operations' — raw JSON Patch escape hatch for title/description edits or any operation the convenience form doesn't cover.

IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT: once a dataset has been created from a schema, XDM forbids breaking changes. Adding field groups is additive and generally safe; removing fields or changing types is not, and Adobe will reject those with a 400.

schemaId.description: The schema's $id or meta:altId. Full URI ($id) form is recommended, e.g. 'https://ns.adobe.com/{tenant}/schemas/abc123...'

addFieldGroupRefs.description: Convenience: field group $ref URIs to APPEND to the schema. Each becomes an { op:'add', path:'/allOf/-', value:{ $ref } } patch operation. Example: ['https://ns.adobe.com/xdm/context/profile-person-details']

path.description: JSON Pointer path, e.g. '/allOf/-' to append or '/title' to replace

operations.description: Raw JSON Patch operations, applied AFTER any generated from 'addFieldGroupRefs'. Use for title/description changes or anything the convenience form doesn't cover.

tools.name: aep_list_datasets
tools.description:
[Adobe Real-Time CDP · Datasets · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List datasets from the Adobe Experience Platform Catalog. Supports filtering by name (contains-match) and state. Returns an array of datasets keyed by id. Filters are sent via Adobe's 'property=field==value' (or 'field~value' for contains) syntax; when both name and state are supplied, they are sent as repeated 'property' parameters and AND-combined server-side.

PAGINATION: Adobe Catalog uses opaque cursor pagination — the 'start' query param is a dataset-ID cursor, not a numeric offset. Use 'limit' to control page size, and pass the 'nextCursor' returned by a prior call as 'startCursor' to fetch the next page.

Requires entitlement: Real-Time CDP

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100)

startCursor.description: Opaque cursor from previous response's _page.next, for pagination beyond first page

name.description: Optional case-sensitive contains-match filter on dataset name

tools.name: aep_get_dataset
tools.description:
[Adobe Real-Time CDP · Datasets · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Get a single dataset by ID from the Adobe Experience Platform Catalog. Returns the full dataset definition including schema reference, tags, and file descriptor.

Requires entitlement: Real-Time CDP

datasetId.description: The dataset ID, a 24-character hex string (example from Adobe's docs: '5e8c91e8c4f9a818a8b3a5e1')

tools.name: aep_create_dataset
tools.description:
[Adobe Real-Time CDP · Datasets · write · Sandbox-scoped]

Create a new dataset in the Adobe Experience Platform Catalog backed by an XDM schema. Optionally enables the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile ingestion. Returns the created dataset ID.

Requires entitlement: Real-Time CDP

name.description: Human-readable name for the dataset (e.g. 'Loyalty Events')

description.description: Optional description of the dataset's purpose

schemaRef.description: The $id of the XDM schema this dataset will conform to

enabledForProfile.description: When true, tags the dataset for Real-Time Customer Profile ingestion (unifiedProfile=enabled:true)

tools.name: aep_delete_dataset
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Datasets · delete · Sandbox-scoped]

DESTRUCTIVE: Permanently deletes an Adobe Experience Platform dataset and all data it contains. This CANNOT be undone. Adobe provides no restore.

DRY RUN BY DEFAULT: dryRun defaults to TRUE. A real deletion requires BOTH dryRun=false and the id-bound confirmation below.

REQUIRED CONFIRMATION: callers MUST pass 'confirm' set to the EXACT string 'DELETE DATASET <datasetId>', naming the same id being deleted. A generic phrase is not accepted — the confirmation is bound to the specific dataset so a copy-pasted confirmation cannot authorise deleting a different one. If allowProfileEnabled=true, the required phrase instead becomes 'DELETE PROFILE-ENABLED DATASET <datasetId>'.

PREFLIGHT: the dataset is fetched and inspected before any DELETE is issued. Datasets that are Profile-enabled, system-managed, or application-managed are REFUSED by default, because those are usually shared infrastructure rather than something a caller created.

Set dryRun=true to run the preflight and return the request that WOULD be sent, without issuing any DELETE.

NOT YET LIVE-VALIDATED: request shape follows Adobe's Catalog API. No dataset has been deleted with this tool against a live tenant.

DESTRUCTIVE: this operation cannot be undone.

datasetId.description: The exact id of the dataset to delete, as returned by aep_create_dataset or aep_list_datasets. Must be an exact id — this tool never resolves a target by name.

confirm.description: Required when dryRun is false. Must equal exactly 'DELETE DATASET <datasetId>' for the same id passed above.

dryRun.description: DEFAULTS TO TRUE. A real deletion must be asked for explicitly by passing dryRun=false AND the id-bound confirmation. When true, runs the preflight and returns the DELETE that would be sent, without sending it.

allowProfileEnabled.description: Escape hatch to permit deleting a Profile-enabled dataset. Off by default: deleting one removes data from Real-Time Customer Profile and can break downstream audiences. Setting this ALSO changes the required confirmation to 'DELETE PROFILE-ENABLED DATASET <datasetId>'.

tools.name: aep_list_identity_namespaces
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Identities · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List identity namespaces registered in the Adobe Experience Platform Identity Service. Returns both standard (ECID, email, phone, etc.) and custom namespaces for the tenant. Use the optional 'custom' flag to filter to only tenant-defined custom namespaces.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100)

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination

custom.description: If true, return only custom (tenant-defined) namespaces. If false or omitted, return all namespaces.

tools.name: aep_get_identity_graph
tools.description:
[Adobe Real-Time CDP · Identities · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Retrieve the identity graph (cluster) for a given identity from the Adobe Experience Platform Identity Service. Returns all linked identities across namespaces (ECID, email, phone, CRM ID, etc.) that resolve to the same person/entity. Provide the identity value and either a namespace code (e.g. 'ECID', 'email', 'phone') or a numeric namespace ID. If neither is provided, the namespace code defaults to 'ECID'.

Requires entitlement: Identity Service / Real-Time CDP

identityValue.description: The identity value to look up (e.g. an ECID like '12345678901234567890', an email address, or a CRM ID).

namespaceCode.description: Namespace code for the identity (e.g. 'ECID', 'email', 'phone', 'CRMID'). Defaults to 'ECID' if neither namespaceCode nor namespaceId is supplied.

namespaceId.description: Numeric namespace ID (alternative to namespaceCode). If both are provided, namespaceId takes precedence.

tools.name: aep_get_profile
tools.description:
[Adobe Real-Time CDP · Profiles · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Get the full unified profile entity from the Adobe Experience Platform Unified Profile Service (UPS). Returns the merged record including XDM attributes, identity graph, consent, and segment membership. Use a more specific schema name if you need a non-default XDM class (defaults to '_xdm.context.profile').

Requires entitlement: Real-Time CDP

entityId.description: The entity identifier value (e.g. an ECID, email address, or CRM ID).

entityIdNS.description: The namespace code for the entity ID (e.g. 'ECID', 'email', 'phone', 'CRMID').

schemaName.description: XDM schema class name for the entity. Defaults to '_xdm.context.profile' for individual profiles.

tools.name: aep_get_profile_by_identity
tools.description:
[Adobe Real-Time CDP · Profiles · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Retrieve a unified customer profile from the Adobe Experience Platform Real-Time Customer Profile service using any known identity (email, ECID, phone, CRM ID, etc.) and its namespace. Returns the merged profile including attributes, identity graph, consent, and segment membership.

Requires entitlement: Real-Time CDP

identityValue.description: The identity value to look up the profile by (e.g. 'user@example.com', an ECID, a CRM ID).

namespaceCode.description: The namespace code for the provided identity value (e.g. 'email', 'ECID', 'phone', 'CRMID').

tools.name: aep_preview_profile
tools.description:
[Adobe Real-Time CDP · Profiles · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Get an abbreviated preview of a unified profile from the Adobe Experience Platform Unified Profile Service (UPS). Returns only the requested XDM field paths (e.g. 'person.name', 'person.email', 'segmentMembership') to minimize payload size. If no fields are specified, returns only top-level profile attributes (no nested objects).

Requires entitlement: Real-Time CDP

entityId.description: The entity identifier value (e.g. an ECID, email address, or CRM ID).

entityIdNS.description: The namespace code for the entity ID (e.g. 'ECID', 'email').

fields.description: Optional list of XDM field paths to return (e.g. ['person.name', 'person.email', 'segmentMembership']). If omitted, returns only top-level attributes.

tools.name: aep_delete_profile
tools.description:
[Adobe Real-Time CDP · Profiles · delete · Sandbox-scoped]

⚠️ DEPRECATED — PREFER 'aep_create_record_delete'.

Adobe has publicly condemned the endpoint this tool wraps: "The delete entity endpoint will be deprecated by the end of October 2025. If you want to perform record delete operations, you can use the Data Lifecycle record delete API workflow." As of the last documentation check (May 2026) the endpoint still responds and Adobe has published no replacement sunset date — so this tool is retained for tenants where it remains the working path. New integrations should use 'aep_create_record_delete', which targets Adobe's sanctioned Data Lifecycle API.

DESTRUCTIVE: Permanently deletes a unified profile from the Adobe Experience Platform Unified Profile Service (UPS). This call immediately purges the profile entity from the Profile Store and triggers an asynchronous privacy/GDPR job to remove related data across the platform. The deletion CANNOT be undone. Use only for verified privacy/erasure requests (GDPR/CCPA).

REQUIRED CONFIRMATION: callers MUST pass the 'confirm' input set to the EXACT literal string 'I understand this is irreversible'. Any other value, or omitting the field, will reject the call BEFORE any API call is made.

The response includes a JobId when one is returned by UPS, which can be tracked via the Privacy Service.

Requires entitlement: Real-Time CDP DESTRUCTIVE: this operation cannot be undone.

entityId.description: The entity identifier value to delete (e.g. an ECID, email, or CRM ID).

entityIdNS.description: The namespace code for the entity ID (e.g. 'ECID', 'email', 'phone', 'CRMID').

schemaName.description: XDM schema class name for the entity. Defaults to '_xdm.context.profile'. Override only when deleting non-profile entities (e.g. ExperienceEvents).

confirm.description: REQUIRED confirmation gate. Must equal the EXACT literal string: 'I understand this is irreversible'. Any other value rejects the request without making the API call.

tools.name: aep_list_segments
tools.description:
[Adobe Real-Time CDP · Segments · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List segment definitions from the Adobe Experience Platform Unified Profile Service. Returns a paginated list of segments, optionally filtered by state (ACTIVE/INACTIVE/DRAFT) or by a case-insensitive name substring match (filtered client-side after the API call).

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100)

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination

name.description: Optional case-insensitive substring match on segment name

tools.name: aep_get_segment
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Segments · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Get a single segment definition by ID from the Adobe Experience Platform Unified Profile Service. Returns the full segment object including its PQL expression, schema reference, evaluation info, TTL, and state.

tools.name: aep_create_segment
tools.description:
[Adobe Real-Time CDP · Segments · write · Sandbox-scoped]

Create a new segment definition in the Adobe Experience Platform Unified Profile Service. Accepts a PQL expression describing the audience logic, the XDM schema class to evaluate against (defaults to '_xdm.context.profile'), and the evaluation cadence (batch or continuous). Returns the created Segment including its server-assigned id.

Requires entitlement: Real-Time CDP

name.description: Human-readable name for the segment (e.g. 'High Value Customers')

description.description: Optional description of the segment's intent

pqlExpression.description: The PQL (Profile Query Language) expression that defines the segment's audience logic

pqlFormat.description: Format of the PQL expression: 'pql/text' (human-readable) or 'pql/json' (AST)

schemaName.description: XDM schema class the segment evaluates against (defaults to _xdm.context.profile)

ttlInDays.description: Optional time-to-live in days for profile membership in this segment

tools.name: aep_estimate_segment_size
tools.description:
[Adobe Real-Time CDP · Segments · execute · Sandbox-scoped]

Estimate the qualifying audience size for a segment in the Adobe Experience Platform Unified Profile Service. Pass 'segmentId' to estimate an existing segment definition (returns metadata directly from the segment definition, which may include 'estimatedSize'), OR pass 'pqlExpression' to preview the size of a candidate PQL query without persisting it. At least one of the two must be provided. NOTE: The PQL preview flow is asynchronous — it submits a preview, then polls the estimate endpoint up to 12 times with progressive backoff (~75s total budget), since real AEP estimates typically take 15-60 seconds. Responses include 'sizeKnown': when false, 'totalProfileSize' is null meaning the size is UNKNOWN — which is NOT the same as an empty audience.

Requires entitlement: Real-Time CDP

segmentId.description: ID of an existing segment definition to fetch (may include estimatedSize directly)

pqlExpression.description: A PQL/text expression to estimate without persisting a segment definition

tools.name: aep_delete_segment
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Segments · delete · Sandbox-scoped]

DESTRUCTIVE: Permanently delete a segment definition from Adobe Experience Platform. The definition and its evaluation history are removed; profiles are not deleted, but any activation depending on this segment stops resolving.

Until v0.9.1 segments could be created but never removed, so every segment an agent made was permanent. That asymmetry is what this closes.

REQUIRED CONFIRMATION: pass 'confirm' set to the EXACT string 'DELETE SEGMENT <segmentId>', naming the same segment. Any other value rejects the call BEFORE any network request.

EXCEPTION: when 'dryRun' is true (the default) nothing is sent and no confirmation is needed. The dry run is purely LOCAL — it contacts Adobe only to confirm the segment exists.

Deletion is verified by a follow-up GET. Adobe answers DELETE with 200 and an empty body, which is not evidence the definition is gone, so the tool re-reads it and reports what it actually finds.

DESTRUCTIVE: this operation cannot be undone.

segmentId.description: The EXACT id of the single segment definition to delete. Wildcards, 'ALL', and comma-separated lists are REFUSED — this tool acts on one segment.

dryRun.description: DEFAULTS TO TRUE. Resolves the segment and reports what would be deleted without deleting it. Pass false, with 'confirm', to actually delete.

confirm.description: Required when dryRun is false. Must equal exactly 'DELETE SEGMENT <segmentId>'.

tools.name: aep_list_sources
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Sources · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List available source connectors from the Adobe Experience Platform Flow Service catalog. These are connection specifications (templates) for ingesting data from external systems (databases, cloud storage, advertising, marketing platforms, etc.). Returns a paginated list, optionally filtered by category. Filtering for sources is performed client-side against connection-spec attributes (isSource / uiAttributes.flowType) because Adobe's providerId values are opaque GUIDs.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100)

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination

category.description: Optional category filter (e.g. 'database', 'cloudStorage', 'advertising', 'marketing'). Matched case-insensitively against the connector's category.

tools.name: aep_list_dataflows
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Sources · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List dataflows configured in the Adobe Experience Platform Flow Service. Dataflows are running ingestion or activation pipelines connecting a source to a target. Returns a paginated list, optionally filtered by state (ENABLED/DISABLED) or a raw AEP property filter such as 'name==myFlow'. When both 'state' and 'propertyFilter' are supplied, they are sent as repeated 'property' query params and AND-combined server-side by Adobe.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100)

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination

propertyFilter.description: Optional raw AEP Flow Service property filter (e.g. 'name==myFlow' or 'sourceConnectionIds==abc'). When combined with 'state', both are sent as repeated property params (AND semantics).

tools.name: aep_list_destinations
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Destinations · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List available destination connectors from the Adobe Experience Platform Destinations catalog. These are connection specifications (templates) for activating audiences to external systems (advertising platforms, email/SMS, cloud storage, social, etc.). Returns a paginated list, optionally filtered by category. Filtering for destinations is performed client-side against connection-spec attributes (isDestination / uiAttributes.flowType) because Adobe's providerId values are opaque GUIDs.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100)

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination

category.description: Optional category filter (e.g. 'advertising', 'email', 'social', 'cloudStorage'). Matched case-insensitively against the connector's category.

tools.name: aep_create_destination_connection
tools.description:
[Adobe Real-Time CDP · Destinations · write · Sandbox-scoped]

Create a target (destination) connection in the Adobe Experience Platform Flow Service. This produces the 'destinationConnectionId' that 'aep_activate_segment' requires — without it, activation cannot be performed through this server at all.

TYPICAL FLOW:
  1. aep_list_destinations         -> find the destination and its connectionSpec id
  2. aep_create_destination_connection (this tool) -> get a destinationConnectionId
  3. aep_activate_segment          -> activate an audience to it

The 'params' object is destination-specific (S3 bucket + prefix, an ad platform account id, an API endpoint, etc.). Consult the destination's page in Adobe's documentation for its required shape. If credentials are needed, create the base connection in the AEP UI first and pass its 'baseConnectionId' here.

Requires entitlement: Real-Time CDP

name.description: Human-readable name for the destination connection

description.description: Optional description of what this connection is for

connectionSpecId.description: The destination's connection spec ID. Obtain it from 'aep_list_destinations' — it appears as the destination catalog entry's connectionSpec.id.

baseConnectionId.description: Optional ID of an existing base connection holding the destination's credentials. Required for destinations that authenticate (most ad platforms and cloud storage). Create it in the AEP UI under Destinations > Accounts if you don't have one.

params.description: Destination-specific parameters. Shape varies per destination — e.g. { bucketName, path } for Amazon S3, or { accountId } for an ad platform. See the destination's Adobe documentation page.

dataFormat.description: Output data format for file-based destinations. Ignored by streaming destinations.

tools.name: aep_activate_segment
tools.description:
[Adobe Real-Time CDP · Destinations · execute · Sandbox-scoped]

Activate a segment (audience) to a pre-configured destination connection in the Adobe Experience Platform Flow Service. Creates a new activation flow linking the customer's AEP profile source connection to the destination connection, using the standard profile-to-destination flowSpec.

PREREQUISITES (BOTH must already exist in AEP):
  1. sourceConnectionId — the customer's AEP profile source connection (typically auto-provisioned
     per sandbox; visible under Sources > Accounts in the AEP UI).
  2. destinationConnectionId — the destination connection for the target system. Create via the
     AEP Destinations UI or the connections API before calling this tool.

Optionally accepts a flow name, description, and a schedule (frequency + startTime). Returns the created flow's id and status.

Requires entitlement: Real-Time CDP

segmentId.description: ID of the segment (audience) to activate

sourceConnectionId.description: REQUIRED: ID of the pre-existing AEP profile source connection. This is the customer's Unified Profile source connection that supplies profile data to the activation flow. It is typically auto-provisioned per sandbox — find it under Sources > Accounts in the AEP UI.

destinationConnectionId.description: REQUIRED: ID of the destination connection this segment should be sent to. Create one with 'aep_create_destination_connection' (which returns this ID), or use an existing connection configured in the AEP UI under Destinations > Browse.

name.description: Optional human-readable name for the activation flow

description.description: Optional description for the activation flow

frequency.description: Activation cadence. Adobe-accepted values: minute, hour, day, week, month, once.

startTime.description: Optional ISO-8601 timestamp for the first activation run. Converted to epoch SECONDS (string) before sending to Adobe.

tools.name: aep_run_query
tools.description:
[AEP Query Service · Query Service · execute · Sandbox-scoped]

Submit a SQL query to the Adobe Experience Platform Query Service against the data lake. This is an ASYNCHRONOUS operation: the response contains the query 'id' and an initial 'state' (typically QUEUED or RUNNING) but NOT the result rows. Use 'aep_get_query_status' with the returned queryId to poll for completion and retrieve results once 'state' is SUCCESS.

Requires entitlement: Query Service

sql.description: The SQL query to execute against the data lake (PostgreSQL-compatible dialect). Example: SELECT * FROM my_dataset LIMIT 10

name.description: Optional friendly name for the query (helps identify it in query history)

description.description: Optional human-readable description of what the query does

dbName.description: Target database name in '{sandbox}:{database}' form. Defaults to '<configured sandbox>:all', derived from AEP_SANDBOX_NAME — the main data lake DB for the sandbox this server is scoped to. Override only to target a different database.

tools.name: aep_get_query_status
tools.description:
[AEP Query Service · Query Service · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Get the current status of a previously submitted AEP Query Service query by its ID. Returns the Query metadata object including state (QUEUED/RUNNING/SUCCESS/FAILED/CANCELED), rowCount, resultLocation, and any errors. If the query is still RUNNING or QUEUED, the response includes a hint to poll again.

RESULT DATA IS NOT FETCHED BY THIS TOOL. Adobe Query Service returns row-level results via a PostgreSQL-compatible interface, NOT through the REST API. To retrieve actual result rows, connect to Adobe's Query Service PostgreSQL endpoint using the connection credentials shown in the AEP UI (Queries > Credentials). This tool returns query metadata and status only.

Requires entitlement: Query Service

tools.name: aep_list_queries
tools.description:
[AEP Query Service · Query Service · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List queries submitted to the Adobe Experience Platform Query Service for the active sandbox. Supports filtering by state (QUEUED/RUNNING/SUCCESS/FAILED/CANCELED), excluding system/hidden queries, ordering (e.g. '-created' for newest first), and an ISO 'startTime' filter that maps to Adobe's 'start' query param.

PAGINATION: Adobe Query Service uses cursor-based pagination, NOT offset-based. To page through results, pass the 'nextCursor' value returned by a previous call as the 'cursor' input on the next call. The 'start' query param in Adobe's API is an ISO timestamp filter (mapped here from 'startTime'), NOT a row offset.

Requires entitlement: Query Service

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100)

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor. Pass the 'nextCursor' value returned by a previous call to fetch the next page. Omit to start from the beginning.

startTime.description: Optional ISO-8601 timestamp filter — only queries created at or after this time are returned. Maps to Adobe's 'start' query parameter.

state.description: Filter by query state. Omit to list queries in all states.

excludeHidden.description: Hide system-generated queries (recommended). Set false to include hidden queries.

orderby.description: Sort order field. Prefix with '-' for descending. Defaults to '-created' (newest first). Examples: '-created', 'created', '-updated'.

tools.name: aep_create_privacy_job
tools.description:
[Adobe Privacy Service · Privacy · write · Sandbox-scoped]

Submit a new privacy job to the Adobe Privacy Service for GDPR/CCPA/CPRA/etc. data subject requests (access or delete). Adobe Privacy Service coordinates processing across Adobe products (Experience Platform, Analytics, Audience Manager, etc.) on behalf of the company.

Required fields: 'regulation' (jurisdiction code), 'companyContexts' (company-level identifiers such as imsOrgID), and 'users' (one or more user records each carrying an internal key, requested action(s), and identity values).

The response contains a requestId plus per-user jobIds that can be tracked via aep_get_privacy_job, aep_get_privacy_job_results, or cancelled via aep_cancel_privacy_job while still pending.

Requires entitlement: Adobe Privacy Service

regulation.description: Privacy regulation code under which the request is being made (e.g. 'gdpr', 'ccpa', 'cpra_usa', 'vcdpa_va_usa'). Must be one of the codes supported by Adobe Privacy Service.

users.description: Users to process — each with action(s) and identity values

include.description: Adobe product names to include (e.g., ['AdobeCloudPlatform', 'Analytics', 'AudienceManager']). Defaults to all entitled products.

analyticsDeleteMethod.description: How Adobe Analytics handles deletion. anonymize keeps event data minus identifiers; purge removes events entirely.

tools.name: aep_get_privacy_job
tools.description:
[Adobe Privacy Service · Privacy · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Get the current status and details of a single Adobe Privacy Service job by its jobId. Returns regulation, action, submission/modification dates, per-product processing responses, and overall status (submitted/processing/complete/error/cancelled). Use this to poll a job after submitting via aep_create_privacy_job.

Requires entitlement: Adobe Privacy Service

jobId.description: Privacy job ID returned from aep_create_privacy_job

tools.name: aep_list_privacy_jobs
tools.description:
[Adobe Privacy Service · Privacy · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List Adobe Privacy Service jobs for a given regulation. The 'regulation' parameter is REQUIRED by the Adobe Privacy Service API — jobs cannot be queried across regulations in a single call. Optionally filter by status. Returns a paginated list of PrivacyJob records.

Requires entitlement: Adobe Privacy Service

regulation.description: Privacy regulation code to list jobs for (e.g. 'gdpr', 'ccpa', 'cpra_usa'). REQUIRED by Adobe Privacy Service — calls without this are rejected.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100)

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination

tools.name: aep_cancel_privacy_job
tools.description:
[Adobe Privacy Service · Privacy · execute · Sandbox-scoped]

Cancel a pending Adobe Privacy Service job. Cancellation only succeeds while the job is still in 'submitted' or 'processing' state — jobs that have already completed cannot be reversed (use aep_get_privacy_job first to confirm the current status). Cancellation is auditable in Adobe Privacy Service.

Requires entitlement: Adobe Privacy Service

jobId.description: Privacy job ID to cancel. Obtain from aep_create_privacy_job or aep_list_privacy_jobs.

tools.name: aep_get_privacy_job_results
tools.description:
[Adobe Privacy Service · Privacy · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Fetch the results bundle for a completed Adobe Privacy Service job. For 'access' actions the response includes a 'downloadURL' (typically a short-lived signed URL) carrying the exported personal data. For 'delete' actions the response summarises per-product processing status. Only meaningful once the job has reached 'complete' status — poll aep_get_privacy_job first.

Requires entitlement: Adobe Privacy Service

jobId.description: Privacy job ID whose results should be retrieved. Job must be in 'complete' status.

tools.name: aep_list_privacy_namespaces
tools.description:
[Adobe Privacy Service · Privacy · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List the identity namespaces supported by Adobe Privacy Service for the current org. Use this to discover which 'namespace' values are valid for the 'userIDs' field of aep_create_privacy_job. Includes both standard namespaces (e.g. 'email', 'ECID') and any custom namespaces registered for the org. Pagination is applied client-side as Adobe may return a flat array.

Requires entitlement: Adobe Privacy Service

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100)

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination

tools.name: aep_create_batch
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Ingestion · write · Sandbox-scoped]

Create a new batch for ingesting data into an Adobe Experience Platform dataset. This is step 1 of 3 in the AEP batch ingestion flow: create the (empty) batch here, upload one or more files into it with aep_upload_batch_file, then seal it with aep_complete_batch to hand it off for processing. Nothing is ingested until the batch is completed. Returns the created batch including its server-assigned `id`, which every subsequent call in the flow requires. The file format declared here must match the files you upload — a batch created as `json` will fail validation if you upload Parquet.

datasetId.description: The target dataset ID to ingest into (as returned by aep_list_datasets). The dataset's XDM schema determines which records will validate.

format.description: File format of the data being uploaded. 'json' expects newline-delimited JSON (one XDM record per line) — this is the most common choice. 'parquet' expects Parquet files conforming to the dataset schema. 'csv' requires the dataset to be configured for CSV ingestion.

tools.name: aep_upload_batch_file
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Ingestion · write · Sandbox-scoped]

Upload a data file into an existing Adobe Experience Platform ingestion batch. This is step 2 of 3 in the AEP batch ingestion flow (aep_create_batch → this → aep_complete_batch). Provide the data EITHER as `localFilePath` (read from disk, for real data files) OR as `content` (an inline string, for small or generated payloads) — exactly one of the two. Records must be valid XDM conforming to the target dataset's schema; for the 'json' batch format that means newline-delimited JSON, one record per line. Call this once per file, then call aep_complete_batch — nothing is ingested until the batch is completed.

batchId.description: The batch ID returned by aep_create_batch

datasetId.description: The dataset ID this batch targets — must match the datasetId used to create the batch

fileName.description: Name to store the file under within the batch (e.g. 'profiles.json'). Must be a bare file name, not a path — no '/', '\', or '..' segments.

localFilePath.description: Absolute path to a local file to upload. Mutually exclusive with `content`. Maximum 100 MB.

content.description: Inline file content to upload as UTF-8. Mutually exclusive with `localFilePath`. Use for small or model-generated payloads; use `localFilePath` for real data files.

dryRun.description: DEFAULTS TO TRUE. Returns the request that would be sent — method, path, headers, and byte count — without transmitting anything. Pass false to actually upload. The file content itself is never echoed back, only its size and a hash.

tools.name: aep_complete_batch
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Ingestion · execute · Sandbox-scoped]

Signal that all files have been uploaded to an Adobe Experience Platform ingestion batch and hand it off for processing. This is step 3 of 3 in the AEP batch ingestion flow (aep_create_batch → aep_upload_batch_file → this). Until this is called, uploaded files sit in the batch and no data reaches the dataset or Real-Time Customer Profile. Completion is one-way: a completed batch cannot accept further files, so upload everything first. Processing is asynchronous — poll aep_get_batch_status to watch the batch move through loading/staging to success or failure.

batchId.description: The batch ID to mark complete, as returned by aep_create_batch. All files must already be uploaded — no further uploads are accepted after this call.

dryRun.description: DEFAULTS TO TRUE. Returns the request that would be sent without sending it. Pass false, together with the confirmation, to actually complete the batch.

confirm.description: Required when dryRun is false. Must equal exactly 'COMPLETE BATCH <batchId>' for the same id. Bound to the id so a confirmation cannot be reused for a different batch.

tools.name: aep_get_batch_status
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Ingestion · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Get the processing status and metrics of an Adobe Experience Platform ingestion batch. Use this to poll a batch after aep_complete_batch — ingestion is asynchronous and a batch typically moves loading → staging → success over seconds to minutes depending on size. Terminal states are 'success' (data is in the dataset), 'failure' (validation or processing failed — check the `errors` field), and 'abandoned' (created but never completed). Also returns metrics including input/output record counts, so a batch that reports 'success' with a failedRecordCount above zero can be spotted as a partial load.

batchId.description: The batch ID to check, as returned by aep_create_batch

tools.name: aep_list_batches
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Ingestion · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List Adobe Experience Platform ingestion batches for the current sandbox. Optionally filter to a single dataset with `dataSet` or to a lifecycle state with `status`. Use this to audit what has been ingested into a dataset, to find recent failures (status: 'failure'), or to spot batches that were created and uploaded to but never completed (status: 'abandoned'). Each batch includes its status and record-count metrics. Returns a paginated list.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100)

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination

dataSet.description: Optional dataset ID to restrict results to batches ingested into that dataset

status.description: Optional lifecycle state filter. 'success' means the data landed, 'failure' means processing failed, 'abandoned' means the batch was never completed.

tools.name: aep_abort_batch
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Ingestion · write · Sandbox-scoped]

Cancels an in-flight Adobe Experience Platform ingestion batch.

POST /data/foundation/import/batches/{batchId}?action=ABORT

Only works while the batch is still processing. Once a batch reaches a terminal state (success, failed, or already aborted) Adobe will not cancel it.

ABORT and REVERT are ALTERNATIVES, not a sequence. Adobe's guidance: a batch in progress should be ABORTed; a batch that has been successfully mastered should be REVERTed. Verified live 2026-08-15: calling REVERT on an already-aborted batch returns 428 ERR-BI-104. 'aborted' is itself the terminal state for a cancelled batch — do not expect to follow it with a revert.

dryRun defaults to TRUE.

batchId.description: The exact id of the batch, as returned by aep_create_batch or aep_list_batches.

dryRun.description: DEFAULTS TO TRUE. Returns the request that would be sent without sending it. Pass false to actually perform the action.

tools.name: aep_revert_batch
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Ingestion · delete · Sandbox-scoped]

DESTRUCTIVE: Deletes an Adobe Experience Platform ingestion batch and reverts any data it ingested.

POST /data/foundation/import/batches/{batchId}?action=REVERT

Adobe marks the batch 'inactive', which makes it eligible for garbage collection; it is later collected asynchronously and marked 'deleted'. So 'inactive' is the expected immediate outcome — do NOT wait for 'deleted' before proceeding.

USE THIS FOR A COMPLETED BATCH, NOT AN ABORTED ONE. ABORT and REVERT are alternatives. Reverting an already-aborted batch returns 428 ERR-BI-104 (verified live 2026-08-15).

REQUIRED CONFIRMATION when dryRun is false: 'REVERT BATCH <batchId>', naming the same id.

dryRun defaults to TRUE.

DESTRUCTIVE: this operation cannot be undone.

batchId.description: The exact id of the batch, as returned by aep_create_batch or aep_list_batches.

dryRun.description: DEFAULTS TO TRUE. Returns the request that would be sent without sending it. Pass false to actually perform the action.

confirm.description: Required when dryRun is false. Must equal exactly 'REVERT BATCH <batchId>'.

tools.name: aep_create_record_delete
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Data Hygiene · delete · Sandbox-scoped]

DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE: Submit a record delete work order to the Adobe Experience Platform Data Lifecycle API, permanently deleting every record matching the supplied identities from ONE dataset.

A work order CANNOT BE CANCELLED once submitted. Completion may take up to 30 days (15 with Privacy and Security Shield). Documented statuses: received, validated, submitted, ingested, completed, failed. Note that the request action is 'delete_identity' while Adobe reports 'identity-delete' in responses.

datasetId 'ALL' is REFUSED. Comma-separated lists, wildcards, and production sandbox names are refused. One exact dataset id only.

PREFLIGHT: the dataset and its XDM schema are read first. Adobe only deletes records from datasets whose schema defines a primary identity or identityMap, so a dataset without one is refused rather than submitted to no effect. A dataset with an active expiration is also refused.

dryRun DEFAULTS TO TRUE and contacts Adobe not at all. A real submission needs dryRun=false plus confirm='DELETE RECORDS <datasetId> <digest>', where the digest is a hash of the identity set returned by the dry run — so a confirmation cannot survive a change to the identities.

Identity values are never logged, echoed, or returned. Only counts, namespace codes, and the digest appear in output.

This is Adobe's sanctioned replacement for the deprecated delete-entity endpoint wrapped by aep_delete_profile.

NOT LIVE-VALIDATED: contract-verified against Adobe's documentation and mock-tested. Deliberately never executed against a live tenant.

Requires entitlement: Data Hygiene DESTRUCTIVE: this operation cannot be undone.

datasetId.description: The EXACT id of the single dataset to delete records from. 'ALL' is REFUSED — it targets every dataset in the organization, which in a shared sandbox reaches other tenants' data. Comma-separated lists, wildcards, and production sandbox names are also refused. One exact id only.

namespace.description: Identity namespace code for the ID (e.g. 'ECID', 'email', 'phone', 'CRMID'). Must be a namespace registered in the sandbox.

id.description: The identity value to delete (e.g. the ECID, email address, or CRM ID itself).

identities.description: One or more identities whose records should be deleted. Every record in scope that carries any of these identities is permanently removed. Adobe accepts up to 100,000 per work order, and recommends batching toward that ceiling rather than issuing many small orders.

displayName.description: Optional human-readable name for the work order, shown in the Data Hygiene UI.

description.description: Optional free-text description of why the deletion was requested (e.g. a DSR ticket ID).

dryRun.description: DEFAULTS TO TRUE. Runs the preflight and returns the request that WOULD be sent — with identity values REDACTED — and contacts Adobe not at all. A real submission requires dryRun=false plus the confirmation below.

confirm.description: Required when dryRun is false. Must equal exactly 'DELETE RECORDS <datasetId> <digest>', where <digest> is the identity digest returned by the dry run. Binding the confirmation to BOTH the dataset and a hash of the identity set means a confirmation cannot be reused after the identity list changes.

tools.name: aep_get_work_order_status
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Data Hygiene · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Get the current status of an Adobe Experience Platform Data Hygiene work order — the asynchronous job created by aep_create_record_delete. Returns the work order's status (e.g. received, validating, processing, completed, failed), the dataset it targets, how many records it covers, and per-product status details where Adobe reports them.

Record deletes can take hours to reach 'completed'. Poll this tool rather than assuming a submitted work order has already purged the data.

NOTE: this endpoint shape comes from Adobe's published Data Lifecycle API documentation and has not been exercised against a live sandbox — validate the path against your own sandbox before relying on it in production.

Requires entitlement: Data Hygiene

workorderId.description: The work order ID returned by aep_create_record_delete (or listed by aep_list_work_orders).

tools.name: aep_list_work_orders
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Data Hygiene · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List Adobe Experience Platform Data Hygiene work orders for the current sandbox. Work orders are the asynchronous record-delete jobs created by aep_create_record_delete. Returns a paginated list with each work order's ID, action, target dataset, status, and timestamps.

Use this to audit what deletions have been requested in a sandbox, or to recover a workorderId for aep_get_work_order_status.

NOTE: this endpoint shape comes from Adobe's published Data Lifecycle API documentation and has not been exercised against a live sandbox — validate the path and query parameters against your own sandbox before relying on it in production.

Requires entitlement: Data Hygiene

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100)

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination

status.description: Optional status filter (e.g. 'received', 'processing', 'completed', 'failed'). Omit to return work orders in every status.

action.description: Optional action filter (e.g. 'delete_identity', 'delete_dataset'). Omit to return work orders for every action.

tools.name: aep_create_dataset_expiration
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Data Hygiene · write · Sandbox-scoped]

DESTRUCTIVE: Set a dataset expiration (TTL) on an Adobe Experience Platform dataset via the Data Hygiene API. At the expiry timestamp Adobe permanently deletes the dataset and all of its data — the deletion CANNOT be undone once it executes. Setting an expiration on a dataset that already has one replaces the existing schedule.

REQUIRED CONFIRMATION: callers MUST pass 'confirm' set to the EXACT string 'CREATE DATASET EXPIRATION <datasetId>', naming the same dataset. Any other value, or omitting the field, rejects the call BEFORE any API call is made.

EXCEPTION: when 'dryRun' is true the confirmation is NOT required, because nothing is sent. IMPORTANT: Adobe does NOT document a dry-run mode for dataset expiration. dryRun here is a purely LOCAL preview — it returns the exact request that would be sent and contacts Adobe not at all. It confirms request SHAPE only; it does not confirm Adobe would accept it.

Uses POST /data/core/hygiene/ttl with datasetId in the body, per Adobe's published API.

NOT YET LIVE-VALIDATED: the request shape follows Adobe's documentation but no expiration has been created against a live tenant from this tool.

Requires entitlement: Data Hygiene DESTRUCTIVE: this operation cannot be undone.

datasetId.description: The ID of the dataset to schedule for deletion. The whole dataset — not a subset of its records — is deleted when the expiry is reached.

expiry.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which the dataset should be deleted, e.g. '2027-01-01T00:00:00Z'. Must be in the future; Adobe rejects past timestamps.

displayName.description: REQUIRED by Adobe. Human-readable name for the expiration, shown in the Data Hygiene UI. Was optional here until 2026-08-16, which would have produced a request Adobe rejects — verified against the Dataset Expiration API documentation.

description.description: Optional free-text description of why the dataset is being expired (e.g. a retention policy ID).

dryRun.description: When true, return the request that WOULD be sent without contacting Adobe at all. Nothing is created and the 'confirm' gate is skipped. Note that Adobe does not offer a server-side dry run for this endpoint, so this validates shape only, not acceptance.

confirm.description: Required when dryRun is false. Must equal exactly 'CREATE DATASET EXPIRATION <datasetId>' for the same dataset id. Ignored when dryRun is true.

tools.name: aep_list_dataset_expirations
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Data Hygiene · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List the dataset expirations (TTLs) configured in the current sandbox via the Adobe Experience Platform Data Hygiene API. Each entry shows the dataset, the ISO 8601 timestamp at which it is scheduled for deletion, and the current status of that schedule.

Use this to audit which datasets are on a delete clock before data disappears, and to recover the datasetId needed to change or extend a TTL with aep_create_dataset_expiration.

NOTE: this endpoint shape comes from Adobe's published Data Lifecycle API documentation and has not been exercised against a live sandbox — validate the path and query parameters against your own sandbox before relying on it in production.

Requires entitlement: Data Hygiene

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100)

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination

datasetId.description: Optional dataset ID filter. Omit to return every configured expiration in the sandbox.

status.description: Optional status filter (e.g. 'pending', 'executing', 'cancelled'). Omit to return expirations in every status.

tools.name: aep_get_dataset_expiration
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Data Hygiene · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Look up a single Adobe Experience Platform dataset expiration.

GET /data/core/hygiene/ttl/{id} — the id may be either a ttlId or a datasetId.

Set includeHistory=true to append ?include=history, which returns a history array of configuration changes. Read-only.

id.description: Either the ttlId (e.g. 'SD-c1f902aa-...') or the datasetId of the expiration.

includeHistory.description: When true, request ?include=history and return the change history.

tools.name: aep_update_dataset_expiration
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Data Hygiene · write · Sandbox-scoped]

Amend a PENDING Adobe Experience Platform dataset expiration.

PUT /data/core/hygiene/ttl/{ttlId} — this endpoint takes the ttlId ONLY, not a datasetId.

At least one of displayName, description, or expiry must be supplied. Adobe permits this only while the expiration's status is 'pending'; the tool reads the current state first and refuses otherwise, naming the actual status.

dryRun DEFAULTS TO TRUE. A real update requires dryRun=false and confirm='UPDATE DATASET EXPIRATION <ttlId>'.

DESTRUCTIVE: this operation cannot be undone.

ttlId.description: The ttlId of the expiration. A datasetId is NOT accepted here.

dryRun.description: DEFAULTS TO TRUE. Returns the request without sending it.

confirm.description: Required when dryRun is false: 'UPDATE DATASET EXPIRATION <ttlId>'.

tools.name: aep_cancel_dataset_expiration
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Data Hygiene · delete · Sandbox-scoped]

Cancel a PENDING Adobe Experience Platform dataset expiration, so the scheduled deletion does not happen.

DELETE /data/core/hygiene/ttl/{id} — the id may be a ttlId or a datasetId.

This is the SAFE direction: it prevents a deletion rather than causing one. Adobe permits it only while status is 'pending'; the tool reads the state first and refuses otherwise. Success is confirmed by a follow-up GET reporting status 'cancelled', not by the response body.

dryRun DEFAULTS TO TRUE. A real cancel requires dryRun=false and confirm='CANCEL DATASET EXPIRATION <id>'.

DESTRUCTIVE: this operation cannot be undone.

id.description: The ttlId or datasetId of the expiration to cancel.

dryRun.description: DEFAULTS TO TRUE. Returns the request without sending it.

confirm.description: Required when dryRun is false: 'CANCEL DATASET EXPIRATION <id>'.

tools.name: aep_get_data_lifecycle_quota
tools.description:
[Adobe Experience Platform · Data Hygiene · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Read Adobe Experience Platform Data Lifecycle quota usage and entitlement.

GET /data/core/hygiene/quota

Optionally filter with quotaType: datasetExpirationQuota, dailyConsumerDeleteIdentitiesQuota, or monthlyConsumerDeleteIdentitiesQuota.

Read-only. Check this before planning record deletes or expirations at volume — both consume a metered allowance.

quotaType.description: Optional filter. Omit to return every quota type.

tools.name: ajo_list_campaigns
tools.description:
[Adobe Journey Optimizer · Campaigns · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List Adobe Journey Optimizer campaigns in the current sandbox. Returns each campaign's id, name, state, schedule and channel, with paging metadata.

AJO is a SEPARATE Adobe product from Experience Platform and is licensed separately. If this returns 403 or 404, the credential's organization is most likely not entitled to Journey Optimizer — that is not a fault in the request.

Paging is 1-based via `page`, with `count` as the page size — NOT limit/offset, which the rest of this server uses. That is Adobe's shape for this endpoint, not a local inconsistency.

Requires entitlement: Adobe Journey Optimizer

page.description: 1-based page number. Adobe's paging here is page/count, not limit/offset.

orderBy.description: Sort field, e.g. 'name' or '-modifiedAt'. A leading '-' reverses the order. Adobe defaults to 'name'.

full.description: When true, ask Adobe for the full campaign representation rather than the list summary. Heavier responses; leave false unless you need the detail for every row.

tools.name: ajo_get_campaign
tools.description:
[Adobe Journey Optimizer · Campaigns · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Get a single Adobe Journey Optimizer campaign by id, including its state, schedule, channel and content references.

AJO is a SEPARATE Adobe product from Experience Platform and is licensed separately. A 403 or a 404 on every id usually means the organization is not entitled to Journey Optimizer.

A 404 for one specific id means that campaign does not exist, or exists with no published version — Adobe distinguishes these with the error code CJMCMP-2044-404, 'The campaign has no acceptable version', which this tool surfaces rather than flattening to 'not found'.

Requires entitlement: Adobe Journey Optimizer

campaignId.description: The AJO campaign id (a UUID, as returned by ajo_list_campaigns).

tools.name: cja_list_companies
tools.description:
[Customer Journey Analytics · Data Views · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Report which Customer Journey Analytics company context this server is using, and attempt Adobe's company discovery.

IMPORTANT: discovery is served by `analytics.adobe.io`, which belongs to Adobe Analytics — a different product from CJA. A credential entitled to CJA but not Analytics gets a 403 there, and CJA exposes no discovery endpoint of its own. When that happens this tool says so explicitly rather than reporting 'no companies', because an entitlement gap and an empty tenant are different problems.

CJA requests work without a company id, scoped by IMS org. Set CJA_GLOBAL_COMPANY_ID to override and send an explicit `x-proxy-global-company-id` header.

Requires entitlement: Customer Journey Analytics

tools.name: cja_list_connections
tools.description:
[Customer Journey Analytics · Data Views · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List Customer Journey Analytics connections. A connection binds CJA to one or more AEP datasets; it is NOT the same thing as an AEP sandbox, and there is no one-to-one mapping between them.

An empty list means the CJA instance has no connections — it is a successful, authorized answer, not a failure.

Requires entitlement: Customer Journey Analytics

limit.description: Results per page (1–100). CJA's own default is 10; this server defaults to 25.

page.description: Zero-based page number. CJA pages from 0, unlike the AEP tools' limit/offset.

nameContains.description: Case-insensitive filter on connection name. Applied CLIENT-SIDE to the requested page only, because CJA does not document a name filter for this endpoint.

tools.name: cja_list_data_views
tools.description:
[Customer Journey Analytics · Data Views · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List Customer Journey Analytics data views. A data view is the reporting lens over a connection — it defines which dimensions and metrics exist for reporting. Every CJA report requires a data view id, so this is usually the first CJA call to make.

Requires entitlement: Customer Journey Analytics

limit.description: Results per page (1–100). CJA's own default is 10; this server defaults to 25.

page.description: Zero-based page number. CJA pages from 0, unlike the AEP tools' limit/offset.

nameContains.description: Case-insensitive filter on data view name. Applied CLIENT-SIDE to the requested page only.

tools.name: cja_list_segments
tools.description:
[Customer Journey Analytics · Data Views · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List Customer Journey Analytics segments (filters). CJA segments are distinct from AEP audiences — they are reporting filters defined inside CJA, not Real-Time CDP audiences.

Served from `/segments`, NOT `/data/segments`.

Requires entitlement: Customer Journey Analytics

limit.description: Results per page (1–100). CJA's own default is 10; this server defaults to 25.

page.description: Zero-based page number. CJA pages from 0, unlike the AEP tools' limit/offset.

nameContains.description: Case-insensitive name filter, applied CLIENT-SIDE to the requested page only.

tools.name: cja_list_calculated_metrics
tools.description:
[Customer Journey Analytics · Data Views · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List Customer Journey Analytics calculated metrics — derived metrics defined in CJA on top of a data view's base metrics.

Served from `/calculatedmetrics`, NOT `/data/calculatedmetrics`, which returns an HTML 404.

Requires entitlement: Customer Journey Analytics

limit.description: Results per page (1–100). CJA's own default is 10; this server defaults to 25.

page.description: Zero-based page number. CJA pages from 0, unlike the AEP tools' limit/offset.

nameContains.description: Case-insensitive name filter, applied CLIENT-SIDE to the requested page only.

tools.name: cja_get_connection
tools.description:
[Customer Journey Analytics · Data Views · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Get one Customer Journey Analytics connection by id, including the AEP datasets it binds.

Requires entitlement: Customer Journey Analytics

connectionId.description: The CJA connection id, as returned by cja_list_connections.

tools.name: cja_get_data_view
tools.description:
[Customer Journey Analytics · Data Views · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Get one Customer Journey Analytics data view by id, with its configuration metadata — owner, parent connection, and timezone.

Requires entitlement: Customer Journey Analytics

dataViewId.description: The CJA data view id (looks like 'dv_...'), as returned by cja_list_data_views.

tools.name: cja_list_dimensions
tools.description:
[Customer Journey Analytics · Data Views · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List the dimensions available in a Customer Journey Analytics data view — the fields you can break a report down by. Requires a data view id, because dimensions only exist within one.

CJA returns the whole list in a single response, so `search`, `limit` and `offset` are applied by this server rather than by Adobe; the output labels that plainly.

Requires entitlement: Customer Journey Analytics

dataViewId.description: REQUIRED. The CJA data view id (e.g. 'dv_...'). Dimensions and metrics only exist within a data view; get one from cja_list_data_views.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring match against id, name and type. Applied after fetching, because CJA returns the full list in one response.

limit.description: Maximum components to return (1–200). Applied client-side; CJA returns the whole list at once.

offset.description: Number of components to skip before returning results. Client-side.

tools.name: cja_list_metrics
tools.description:
[Customer Journey Analytics · Data Views · read · Sandbox-scoped]

List the metrics available in a Customer Journey Analytics data view — the things you can measure. Requires a data view id.

These are the data view's BASE metrics. Metrics derived in CJA are separate; use cja_list_calculated_metrics for those.

Requires entitlement: Customer Journey Analytics

dataViewId.description: REQUIRED. The CJA data view id (e.g. 'dv_...'). Dimensions and metrics only exist within a data view; get one from cja_list_data_views.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring match against id, name and type. Applied after fetching, because CJA returns the full list in one response.

limit.description: Maximum components to return (1–200). Applied client-side; CJA returns the whole list at once.

offset.description: Number of components to skip before returning results. Client-side.

tools.name: cja_run_report
tools.description:
[Customer Journey Analytics · Reporting · read · Sandbox-scoped]

Run a read-only Customer Journey Analytics report and return the rows.

Requires a data view, an explicit date range, one dimension and at least one metric. Dimension and metric ids must be the EXACT ids from cja_list_dimensions and cja_list_metrics — this tool never guesses or substitutes a component, because a report built from a silently-swapped metric returns confident, wrong numbers.

Rows are capped and the date range is bounded: a report is a query against live analytics data, not a bulk export. This is a POST, but it creates nothing.

Requires entitlement: Customer Journey Analytics

dataViewId.description: REQUIRED. The CJA data view to report against (e.g. 'dv_...'). Get one from cja_list_data_views.

startDate.description: REQUIRED. Inclusive start date, YYYY-MM-DD. There is no default — an implicit range would make an expensive query easy to run by accident.

dimension.description: REQUIRED. The dimension id to break the report down by, exactly as returned by cja_list_dimensions (e.g. 'variables.daterangeday'). Not a display name.

metrics.description: REQUIRED. 1–10 metric ids exactly as returned by cja_list_metrics (e.g. 'metrics.occurrences'). Not display names.

segmentIds.description: Optional CJA segment ids to apply as global filters, from cja_list_segments.

limit.description: Rows per page (1–200). Capped deliberately: a report is a query against live analytics data, not a bulk export.

sortDirection.description: Sort direction on the first metric.

instructions: Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) MCP server. All operations scoped to a single sandbox configured at startup. Tool descriptions are prefixed with [Product · Category · operation] metadata for routing. Conventions: inputs validated via zod; errors return as structured tool results (isError: true), never throws; pagination uses offset/limit — check 'hasMore' for completion; destructive ops (delete-profile) require explicit confirmation args; some tools require entitlements beyond base AEP (Real-Time CDP, Query Service) — tagged in descriptions. Recommended schema workflow: aep_list_schemas → aep_create_schema → aep_create_dataset.
